noveltyJustification: Three of six findings are new (the 26-frame ratio survey, the metric+delta gap, the inline-SVG direction cue), two confirm the shipped register, one restates a rationale the contract already records; the angle's central gap is newly evidenced against three independent reference sources.
keyQuestions: Where does our five-part card (headline, subtitle, figure, footer finding, source) read as a template rather than a product, judged against the reference cards' anatomy, typography and spacing?
answeredQuestions: Our furniture (type scale, footer weights, rule, gap) is dimension-identical to the reference, and the only true divergence is figure aspect: 26/26 of our frames run 24.4-55.6% of their 720-unit width (median 43.4%) against the reference's locked 56.25%; the product gap is the missing prominent number in the header zone (metric+delta), which every product-grade reference lead carries.
ruledOut: Header controls, a header border or fixed 12px insets in every card: theirs need a runtime and component library; our eight inert forms and per-form insets are recorded decisions (finding 4).
Any change to card padding, card width or footer weights: dimension-for-dimension parity with the reference footer was confirmed at both sources (finding 6).
Trust the contract prose for the shipped fade: the file says 0.35/0.04 where the prose says 0.8/0.1 (daily-line.html:137-138); promoted to angle 2, not an angle-1 claim.

summary: The 1px-rule, 16/14/12 type scale and footer weights match the reference dimension-for-dimension; the divergence is the figure, not the furniture.
